expected_points: A strong purpose describes the change the company wants to see in the world, independent of financial gain.

answer.summary: Jackson says an effective purpose clearly states the change a company wants to make in the world, gives people a memorable reason it exists, and remains a long-term north star. It can guide decisions, align employees, and give the public a reason to root for the company.

sections.heading: What makes a purpose effective
sections.content: Use a clear “we exist to…” statement about the change the company wants to see in the world, irrespective of financial gain. Jackson favors one memorable purpose—the reason the company does what it does—rather than asking people to retain separate mission and vision statements. It should be durable: she contrasts a purpose that stays roughly the same for 10 years with early-stage product positioning that may evolve on an 18-month frame.

sections.heading: How it can help the company
sections.content: A purpose can act as a north star for company decisions, align employees around a shared reason for their work, and make people want to work for the company and feel part of something. It can also help the public want the company to win. Jackson’s examples illustrate the idea: Google’s purpose was to organize the world’s information and make it universally accessible and useful; she said employees knew it from hiring and onboarding, and it appeared in the offer letter and elsewhere. Stripe’s purpose, “to increase the GDP of the internet,” is related to financial gain, but Jackson still praised it as evocative and able to make people want to root for the company.
